newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Ilie Nastase quits politics after Romania polls.
newsitem.headline: Ilie Nastase quits politics after Romania polls.

text.p: Former tennis star Ilie Nastase has left politics in disgust after being defeated twice in bids for office on behalf of Romanian President Ion Iliescu's leftist party, according to a statement released on Thursday.
"I had been dragged into a political quagmire," Nastase told Romanian media in announcing his resignation from the Party of Social Democracy (PDSR).
"My parents were right to tell me as a child that politics do not marry well with morality."
The one-time winner of the French Open, who returned home this year to seek a role in the Balkan country's politics, was not immediately available for comment.

Nastase lost a race for Bucharest mayor in June and for a seat in parliament in November 3 polls, when Iliescu's leftwingers were removed from government for the first time since the 1989 fall of communism.
The PDSR had picked Nastase, a national hero for his pranks on and off the courts in the 1970s, in a bid to revive their sagging electoral fortunes.
Instead, he came under attack in the local press over his association with the president's party.
"Nastase was great for sports, but he doesn't have the make of a politician," PDSR campaign manager Dan Ghibernea told Reuters. "Politics is much tougher than sport."
Iliescu faces a tough run-off battle to retain the presidency on Sunday against a reformist challenger.
